messages:
Alex K: Quick FYI - saw a spike in "no-billing" hits tied to sampling + compact reordering. Not as big as last week but visible in per-tenant rollups, ~0.4%.
Maya P: Can you paste an example trace/envelope?
Alex K: Sure. Header flow: `X-Billing-Key: tenant_99|tierB` -> edge proxy logs show it -> after compacting we get envelope.root.meta = {}.
Frank H: I looked at compactEnvelope() semantics. It merges attribute maps by preferring the earliest non-null value from spans, then drops span-level attrs. With sampling + reorder a span carrying billing_key can be dropped, so merge loses it.
Liam S: Two engineering directions: change merge to union-with-precedence (keep keys from any span instead of first-only) or guarantee billing_key is promoted into root before sampling. Union increases envelope size.
Sam T: Another idea: compute a stable, short billing_fingerprint at edge (e.g. SHA1(prefix) -> 8b base64) and carry that in the compact envelope instead of full string. Then we can run a separate light-weight lookup to resolve fingerprint->billing_key in the analytics stage. That lowers cardinality impact on indexes.
Maya P: Fingerprint map means one extra lookup to resolve human-readable tenant in pipelines. Is that sync or async? We need to decide on latency/consistency guarantees.
Alex K: We could do a hybrid: persist fingerprint synchronously at edge (tiny fixed length), and attempt an async backfill if resolution missing at ingest. Add a confidence flag `billing.resolution = resolved|approx|missing` so downstream can filter.
Frank H: Implementation notes: 1) edge computes `billing_fp` and adds header `X-Billing-FP`; 2) compactEnvelope() treats `billing_fp` as authoritative and always merges fp union (8 bytes max increase); 3) ingest tries local cache (LRU TTL 5m) then global backfill; 4) emit metric `ingest.billing_fp_unresolved` and tag events with `billing.resolution`.
Liam S: Cost model: storing 8b fingerprint as an indexed field is way cheaper than full tenant string. But we need the lookup table (fp -> full key) stored in a fast KV (redis) with replication. Could be small: #tenants ~ 50k, table ~ 50k * 64 bytes = ~3.2MB + overhead. Cheap.
Sam T: Edge compute: cheap sha1 on header string. We should namespace fp by salt per-region to avoid cross-tenant collisions if we change hash algo. Use `billing_fp = base64url(trunc(sha256(salt + billing_key), 8))`.
Maya P: Product question: will we ever need the raw billing_key in latency-critical routing decisions? If so we must resolve at edge, not backfill.
Alex K: We only use billing key for cost attribution and quota checks in route layer (some features). For quota checks we need it sync; for pure attribution we can backfill. So we need both: edge resolves for quota-enabled routes, fingerprint for general routes.
Frank H: Ok gate by config: `edge.resolve_for_routes = ["/v1/rate-limited"]`, `edge.emit_fp_for = ["/v1/generate", "/v1/embed"]`.
Liam S: Action plan: A) small prototype: edge fp generator + compactEnvelope union logic (non-invasive) B) deploy 48h canary on embed route with fp only C) measure `ingest.billing_fp_unresolved` and overall missing-billing fraction.
ingest-bot: ingest.version=v2 | sampling=10% | fp-unresolved=0.006 | billing-missing=0.004
Maya P: If fp-unresolved < 0.01 and billing-missing drops under 0.05% we consider rollout. Also need docs + analytics changes so dashboards show resolution confidence.
Sam T: I'll prototype fp code tonight and open a draft PR.
Frank H: I'll update compact logic to union fps and add `billing.resolution` tag emission. Also add metric `ingest.billing_fp_lookups` latency histogram.
Liam S: I'll model index/storage delta and KV cost. Short note: redis-cluster with 50k keys is trivial. Add fallback HLL for monitoring cardinality growth.
Alex K: Sounds good. Sam/Frank/Liam please sync and post progress here. I'll create INF-8091 for the canary and set a 48h check-in.
Maya P: Thanks. If we still see >0.1% after canary we do a quick RFC for changing merge semantics to full union + compaction dedupe (bigger index cost, simpler correctness).
Alex K: thanks all :heart:
